quote: We prompt several larger decoder-only LLMs to output a list of turn intervals exhibiting friction ... For each predicted turn interval, the model must provide a brief explanation for the cause of friction.
outputs: natural language explanations of why a turn interval exhibits conversational friction

quote: We evaluate models in the Friction Found and Friction Overlap settings
we ask two non-author Linux experts to annotate the similarity between gold friction explanations and model-generated explanations for 64 instances of friction on a three-point scale

We ask two non-author Linux experts to annotate the similarity between gold friction explanations and model-generated explanations for 64 instances of friction on a three-point scale, marking them as either (1) dissimilar, (2) somewhat similar, or (3) equivalent.

Three computer science undergraduates familiar with Linux annotate conversations by (1) identifying turn intervals which exhibit friction along with explanations and (2) judging the success of overall conversation on a three-point scale.
guideline: marking them as either (1) dissimilar, (2) somewhat similar, or (3) equivalent.
Annotators rate the similarity between model-generated explanations and gold explanations using a three-point scale (dissimilar, somewhat similar, equivalent).

Annotators were instructed to identify turn intervals exhibiting conversational friction and provide explanations, and to judge conversation success on a three-point scale (1: No Progress, 2: Some Progress, 3: Success). Instructions were kept identical to Prompt A.1, which defines friction and success criteria.
